instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the shop lease where you signed. Choose the overseas job or this shop; you said we'd build something together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed as a witness. You've put your name in the witness box too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, witnessed intentions. Which of us is signing as the actual partner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could take the job and send money for the shop. You'd run it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then send the first month's rent. We'll call 'together' your money and my days behind the counter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken my key off the ring like you. Keep the spare or return it; let's settle what you meant by taking space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took mine off because it's bent. I meant one quiet evening, not moving out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, making room for the right key. Shall I get you a replacement?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. One that works. I want to be able to come home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the new key tonight. We'll call last week's space one evening, and leave it there.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed my name on the night rota like you. Take the midnight shift if this shelter matters to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross cancels my shift. You just cancelled yours too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, clearing space to supervise. You take midnight to four and I'll stay available.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll do it if you sit at the desk beside me. We can split the calls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we split them before midnight? I need to be asleep by eleven to supervise properly.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my plant beside your pot on the windowsill. Can this one stay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One small plant, yes. My pot's empty; I'm drying it after washing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a drying place. Both my plants are overwatered, so the second one should come here too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The second one's enormous. It will block the light from the first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then swap their positions at lunchtime. You agreed they can dry here; neither should lose its turn in the sun.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I made the opening bold, just like your edits. Admit that helped the speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I use bold for lines I plan to cut. But yes, leaving your opening made the argument clearer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, testing what survives. The rest of the speech follows that opening, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It follows the argument. I wrote all the examples myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then credit your examples and my argument. You already said the opening made it clear.

cards.title: Hide Inside the Callback
cards.instruction: Use an early harmless detail as the explanation for each new consequence, keeping your own role outside the pattern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I pulled my ribbon when you pulled yours. That pretty ribbon has brought the tent down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I untied a bow on a parcel. Yours was tied to the tent's support rope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, releasing the decoration. Nobody told the ribbon it was holding anything up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The pole fell onto the cake. You need to tell the baker what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her the ribbon brought the pole down. I never touched her cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I tipped my cup when you tipped yours. That's the cup that ruined your letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was watering the plant. You poured yours across the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, emptying before we clear up. The cup shouldn't have been beside the letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now the ink's gone. I can't read the address I need to send the reply.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for the address again: 'A cup caused a delay.' That explains the letter and the late reply.

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked whether it rained all evening. It poured. I pressed the flashing triangle like you did when you slowed down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the hazard-light button, not a brake. Is that why you hit my gate?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, visibility. And yes, the rain made the road very hard to see.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you actually press the brake before the gate?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rain eased just after we reached it. You'd asked whether it lasted all evening; it didn't.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked how lunch was. Excellent soup. I helped myself to cake when you took a piece.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took a crumb to test whether it was baked. Did you cut into the birthday cake?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, checking the texture. The soup had plenty of pepper, since you asked about the food.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There should be twelve slices. How many did you eat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enough pepper to warm you up, but not so much you lose the carrot. That's what made lunch good.
